answer:
Jimmy owns a cube-shaped container with a side length of 10 inches, giving it a total volume of:
\[
10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1000 \text{ cubic inches}
\]
He fills the container halfway with water, which occupies:
\[
\frac{1000}{2} = 500 \text{ cubic inches}
\]
Jimmy then adds ten giant ice cubes, each measuring 2 inches on each side. The volume of one ice cube is:
\[
2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8 \text{ cubic inches}
\]
The total volume of the ten ice cubes is:
\[
10 \times 8 = 80 \text{ cubic inches}
\]
To find the unoccupied volume of the container, we subtract the combined volume of the water and ice from the total volume of the container. Whether considering displacement or not, the total occupied volume is the sum of the water and ice volumes:
\[
500 + 80 = 580 \text{ cubic inches}
\]
Thus, the unoccupied volume is:
\[
1000 - 580 = 420 \text{ cubic inches}
\]

The unoccupied volume of the container is \boxed{420} cubic inches.
